text: Restructure. We are restructuring the commercial desk.
Oversee. I oversee eight people and their accounts.
Coordinate. I coordinate with risk and with legal.
Workflow. We are changing the workflow this quarter.
Priority. Right now, the budget is the priority.
Deadline. The deadline is the end of the month.
Quarter. This quarter is harder than the last one.
Headcount. We are asking for more headcount.
I still do not understand what your team actually does all day.
Fair. Normally we handle the deals: a client asks, we price it, risk approves, legal signs.
And you oversee all of that?
I oversee the commercial side. I do not touch risk. But I coordinate with them every week.
Sounds heavy.
It is, and right now it is worse. We are restructuring the desk, so the workflow changes every ten days.
Are you hiring?
No. That is the problem. We are not getting more headcount this year, and the deadline does not move.
So what is the priority this quarter?
Honestly? Getting to December with the same eight people.
I oversee a commercial desk of eight people.
Normally we handle about forty deals a month.
This quarter we're restructuring the workflow.
The priority right now is closing the budget.
And you? What are you working on?

Quick update on where we are. Normally we close about forty deals a month, and the process is stable. This quarter is not normal. We are running two systems at the same time, because we are migrating the old one, and that is costing us about a day a week. I am not complaining, I am explaining the numbers. We are currently at thirty-one deals, which is below target, and the deadline for the quarter does not move. What we are doing about it: we are freezing all new requests until the migration finishes, and we are asking for two temporary people, not permanent headcount. That is the whole picture. Questions after, please, not during.

Before we start, let me introduce someone. This is Marta. Marta runs operations for a logistics company in Lisbon, so she oversees about sixty people across three warehouses. What is interesting for us is what she is doing this year: they are moving everything to one single system, and she is the person holding that together. She is also, and I am quoting her, permanently tired. Marta, when you get a moment, tell the group about the workflow you are building. I think half the room has the same problem.
